title: Verifiable random functions from one-way functions alone
formal: Does the existence of arbitrary one-way functions imply a standard-model verifiable random function on all lambda-bit inputs with adaptive pseudorandomness and perfect uniqueness even for malformed public keys?
definitions:
The security parameter is lambda, supplied in unary. Efficient algorithms are uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machines; security is against nonuniform probabilistic polynomial-size circuit families with polynomially many oracle queries. A function is negligible if it is eventually smaller than lambda^{-c} for every constant c>0. All message, instance and witness lengths in a security experiment are polynomial in lambda. No random oracle, trusted hardware or additional computational assumption is available.

One-way functions means that a uniformly polynomial-time computable family f_lambda:{0,1}^lambda to {0,1}^{ell(lambda)}, for some polynomially bounded output length ell, exists such that every adversary given f_lambda(U_lambda) finds any x-prime with f_lambda(x-prime)=f_lambda(U_lambda) with only negligible probability. Inverters know lambda and must output a lambda-bit preimage. The function need not be injective or a permutation.

KeyGen(1^lambda) returns a public key pk and secret key sk. Deterministic Eval(sk,x) returns a lambda-bit value for each x in {0,1}^lambda, and Prove(sk,x) returns a proof. Deterministic Verify(pk,x,y,pi) accepts or rejects. Honest evaluations and proofs must be accepted except with negligible probability over key generation and proof randomness. All sizes and runtimes are polynomial in lambda.

Perfect uniqueness requires that for every public-key string of the permitted polynomial length, every x, and any two pairs (y,pi),(y-prime,pi-prime) accepted by Verify, y=y-prime. A malformed key may reject everything. There is no requirement that the proof string itself be unique.

For pseudorandomness, an adversary receives an honest pk and adaptively queries an oracle returning (Eval(sk,x),Prove(sk,x)). It chooses a fresh challenge x-star not previously queried, receives either Eval(sk,x-star) or an independent uniform lambda-bit string, and continues oracle queries excluding x-star. No proof for the challenge is supplied. Its distinguishing advantage must be negligible. The domain has 2^lambda inputs; weak security on randomly selected inputs is insufficient. Non-black-box techniques are allowed, and there is no setup beyond the individual generated key pair.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction with correctness, uniqueness and adaptive-security proofs from arbitrary one-way functions, or refute the unrestricted implication. A black-box separation alone does not rule out constructions using the one-way-function description.
context:
A VRF combines a pseudorandom value with public evidence of its unique evaluation. Classical constructions use assumptions stronger than arbitrary one-way functions.

The weak-VRF work both relaxes input selection and establishes a black-box barrier from one-way permutations; that barrier has a restricted scope.
why: The question tests whether public verifiability requires stronger assumptions than ordinary private pseudorandomness.

import_provenance.original_title: Verifiable random functions from one-way functions alone
import_provenance.original_statement: Do one-way functions suffice to construct fully adaptively secure, publicly verifiable random functions on exponentially large input domains in the standard model? This asks whether the extra algebraic assumptions in constructions such as Dodis–Yampolskiy can be eliminated.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial foundational extension of his VRF work. Known black-box separations from one-way permutations rule out that approach, rather than settling the unrestricted implication.
